en: “I bow to the Mother.
Rich in waters, rich in fruits,
cool with the wind from Malaya,
dark green with crops,
the Mother.
Her nights thrilled by white moonlight,
beautiful with trees in full flower and leaf,
sweetly smiling, sweet of speech,
giver of joy, giver of boons, the Mother.
Terrible with the clamour of seventy million throats,
with sharp swords held in twice seventy million arms,
why, Mother, are you powerless, with so much strength?
Her who holds great strength,
I bow to her who carries us across,
who drives back the hosts of the enemy,
the Mother.
You are knowledge, you are dharma,
you are the heart, you are the inmost core,
for you are the breaths of life in the body.
In the arm, Mother, you are strength,
in the heart, Mother, you are devotion,
it is your image we fashion
in temple after temple.
For you are Durgā, who bears the ten weapons,
Kamalā, who wanders among the lotus petals,
Vāṇī, giver of knowledge;
I bow to you,
I bow to Kamalā,
spotless, peerless,
rich in waters, rich in fruits,
the Mother.
I bow to the Mother,
dark green, upright,
sweetly smiling, adorned,
the earth, who sustains,
the Mother.”
notes: Romanization: ISO 15919 applied to the Bengali script as written, so ব is b throughout (bande, bidyā, dbisapta, tbaṁ, karabāle, baradāṁ); a Sanskrit-style reading of the same words would be vande, vidyā, dvisapta, tvaṁ, karavāle, varadāṁ. Editor: choose whether the site wants the strict Bengali letters or the Sanskrit reading for the Sanskrit lines. ং is ṁ, য় is ẏ, ড় is ṛ, ঋ-kar is r̥, danda | and double danda ||.
line 1.22: তোমারই is tomāra + i (the emphatic -i); ISO 15919's colon (tomāra:i) keeps it apart from the diphthong ai. Pronounced tomari.
line 1.3: malayaja, 'born of Malaya' (the Malabar hills of the south), usually the cool southern breeze; it can also mean sandalwood (cool with sandal paste).
line 1.10-1.11: seventy million (sapta koṭi), twice that many arms: the population of Bengal presidency as Bankim reckoned it. Later versions sing 'thirty crore' for all India; this text has seven.

line 1.12: disputed sense. abalā is 'without strength' and also a common word for 'woman'; eta bale can be 'with so much strength' (bal, strength) or '(why do they) call / say (you are)'. Read either 'why, Mother, are you powerless with so much strength?' or 'who says, Mother, you are weak?'.
line 1.14: tāriṇī, 'she who carries across' (to safety; a name of the goddess as saviour).
line 1.17-1.18, 1.20-1.23 are Bengali; the rest is Sanskrit. 'dharma' is kept untranslated (duty, right order, religion).
line 2.2-2.3: Kamalā is Lakshmi (goddess of fortune, seated on a lotus); Vāṇī is Sarasvatī (goddess of speech and learning).

line 2.10: the text has শ্যামালাং (śyāmālāṁ, with a long ā), where 1.4 has śyāmalāṁ; probably a slip of the edition for śyāmalāṁ 'dark green'. Romanized as written. saralāṁ: 'straight, simple, guileless'; 'upright' is a choice.
line 2.12: ধরনীং is written with dental ন (dharanīṁ) where the Sanskrit word is dharaṇī 'the earth'; romanized as written. bharaṇīm: 'she who supports, nourishes'.
